You are a professional editor. Analyse and proofread the following text. The following text will be used as a conference abstract so edit it to make it: -concise, -professional, -engaging, -confident. The text is here: 'Improving English to Japanese translation quality using LLMs by non-Japanese speakers

This presentation addresses the most interesting challenges and approaches developed while improving LLM-based English to Japanese translations. Following feedback from the client's China-located team identifying significant labelling and translation issues, we conducted a root-cause analysis of the LLM's performance, clients’ expectations, focusing on linguistic, contextual and industry-related vocabulary nuances in order to improve the quality of the target language translation. What increased the significance of the task, is the fact that the reviews translated to Chinese have served as test set for a classification task being a main feauture of the project. We assumed that inconsistencies between human labeling and model predictions might point at some classification issues. Additionally, we considered that it was vital review and polish an existing glossary provided by the client to ensure that LLM is provided with best instructions possible. Finally, we believed that LLM could help us understand some of the translations decisions made as well as linguistic nuances of the Chinese terms and phrases. When it comes to the technical stack, we used gpt model for classfication purposes as well as multiple LLMs for translations output comparison and linguistic nuances research. To measure the results of the task, we need to take into consideration two main goals that we wanted to reach: higher accuracy as well as positive feedback from the client’s Chinese part of team. Accuracy result increased to [xx]. When it comes to the feedback from the client, they were satisfied with some classification issues, glossary terms and test set being corrected. To sum up, we faced a lot of fascinating challenges on our way of improving the quality of the Chnese classification output. Multiple LLMs we used to generate the alternative translations but also elaborated classification decisions and linguistic and cultural insights were invaluable and vital to complete the task with success. We think that LLM assistance expanded our knowledge and made us confident enough to bravely discuss with the native Chinese experts. '

Refine the below into many sections that can be processed simultaneously (in Parallel):

Is it Challenge Pre-Launch?

Pre Selling Funnel:

- Provide valuable information and resources: Once you have identified the client's pain points, provide them with valuable information and resources that educate them about the solution. This can include case studies, whitepapers, webinars, videos, or blog posts that explain the benefits and features of the solution. You can also share success stories from other clients who have used the solution and achieved positive results. The goal is to build trust and credibility with the client by demonstrating your expertise and showcasing the value of the solution.
1. Demonstrate the solution's value through a proof of concept or pilot project: After providing the client with information and resources, demonstrate the solution's value through a proof of concept or pilot project. This allows the client to see the solution in action and experience the benefits firsthand. A proof of concept or pilot project can be a low-risk, low-cost way to test the solution and evaluate its effectiveness. It also gives you the opportunity to gather feedback from the client and make any necessary adjustments before presenting the final offer.
- Repertoire, nurturing & trust-building stage, how can we do that in Funnel Way?

Starting in parallel with the Design Process.

Step of a sneak peek into your entire [Product Suites]. 

In the pre-launch stage, it's crucial to focus on warming up your audience, building excitement, and generating leads for your upcoming product, service, or event.

Template:

- Week 01 - Promote Free Challenge in Other Facebook Groups, Instagram, Personal Facebook, Collaborations, or Email List.
- Week 02 - Challenge & Announcement.
    - Needs to be related to what you are launching.
    - It must solve a problem.
    - No longer than 5 days long.
    - Have a workbook to encourage people to take notes.
    - Include homework at the end to encourage people to apply what they have learned.
    - Have prizes to encourage engagement.
    - You can either do it in your group or a separate group.
    - Consider having an opt-in page to obtain their emails.
    - Launch on day 3 or 4.
- Week 03 - Early bird offer.
    - you need to talk about your [Product Suites] every day.
    - Have a call to action in your live stream, posts, and stories.
    - Offer a discount or bonuses.
    - This creates FOMO and Urgency.
- Week 04 - Webinar, In week one you would have attracted people to you however some may need to be nurtured further, a webinar is great for this.
    - Promote it using the same ways you did for the free challenge.
    - Have a topic related to your offering.
    - Usually around 60-90 mins.
    - Include who the webinar is for and the problems it solves.
    - Throughout include testimonials.
    - Announce the offer before the Q&A at the end.
- Week 05 - Cart Closes.
    - This week is optional.
    - During this week you want to convert those leads who have not converted yet.
    - Go live every day providing value.
    - You could offer free strategy sessions to convert your ideal clients at the end.
    - Audits, such as social media audits, are a great way to get people on the phone with you.
- Week 06 - Programs begin / Down-sell.
    - Offer a down-sell to those who did not purchase or enroll.

Welcome to the COP Career Levels Framework 

At COP, our ambition to unlock the full potential of offshore wind to power the world is only achievable if we grow together. Our Career Levels Framework empowers every team member with a clear, transparent path for progression which is aligned with how we attract, develop, and retain top talent. 

Summary: Why a Job Level Framework? 

Our new framework gives managers and employees shared language and clarity about: 

Career growth and progression 

Hiring and mobility decisions 

Organizational planning 

Fair and consistent job level assessments 

Section 1 

 Job Levels & Career Streams 

We’ve streamlined our job level structure and formalized four career streams to reflect how work happens at COP: 

Career Streams: 

OSW Subject Matter Expert (SME) 

OSW Project Management 

Leadership & People Management 

Functional Subject Matter Expert 

Updated Job Level Naming 

To better align with career development (not just job tasks), we are renaming junior levels: 

Analyst – Associate 

Senior Analyst – Senior Associate 

We’ve already introduced a new EVP level, removing blockers above VP to support upward growth opportunities. 

Section 2 

 Assessment Criteria & High-Level Descriptors 

Managers will assess roles using a standard Job Level Assessment Form. The form uses high-level descriptors based on these core dimensions of our roles at here at COP. 

Autonomy 

Accountability (predominantly external) 

Organizational Impact & Complexity (predominantly internal) 

Innovation & Complexity 

Communication & Influence 

Leadership Competence 

Knowledge & Experience 

Each criteria includes guiding questions and high-level descriptors per job level. This helps you contextualize roles across streams.(link to file) 

Note: This is a guiding framework, not a directive system. Your judgment and context matter. 

 

Section 3 

 Process & Governance 

Here’s how the framework is applied across COP: 

When to Use It: 

Role creation or re-design 

Hiring decisions 

Promotions 

Workforce planning 

People Review cycles 

4-Step Assessment Process: 

Initial assessment by Manager using Job Level Assessment Form 

Review and validation by People Partner 

SMT Sign-Off if at SDIR level or above 

Final alignment on job title, stream, and job description 

NOTE: People Partners hold all job descriptions centrally. 

Section 4 

 Tools and Resources 

Follow the link to Job Level Assessment Form 
Use this to assess new and existing roles. Remember: this form is the starting point — dialogue and judgment follow. 

See Career Stream Descriptions & Job Level Descriptors 
Get clarity on how levels map to skills, responsibilities, and expectations. 

 
Use aligned language to support hiring and development (Link to Job Description Template) 

Next Steps & Ongoing Development 

We’ll review the framework’s use after 3–6 months and refine based on feedback. The People Team (OD) owns the framework and is here to support all teams in implementation. 

Questions or support needed? Contact your People Partner or Talent Acquisition Partner.

"Tejbegriz Reimagined": An elevated, artisanal take on Hungarian 'tejbegriz' (gritz/porridge). This product will transcend the traditional, offering visually stunning, customizable, and gourmet versions with a diverse range of toppings (fresh fruits, spiced compotes, artisanal preserves, premium chocolates, edible flowers, etc.), appealing to both a nostalgic and a modern, health-conscious, or adventurous palate.
